statement.text:
Let n ∈ N. Is it true that for every k ∈ {1, . . . , n!} there is some group G and
pairwise distinct elements g1 , . . . , gn ∈ G such that the set {gσ(1) · · · gσ(n) | σ ∈ Sn }
of all products of the gi obtained by permuting the factors has cardinality k? S. Kohl
  ∗ Yes, it is true (P. Monticone, Preprint, 2026, https://kourovkanotebookorg.
wordpress.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/18_50.pdf;
see also S. Kohl’s post at https://mathoverflow.net/questions/123890/
numbers-of-distinct-products-obtained-by-permuting-the-factors/
511354#511354).
